title: The Reliable Classic
description: You don't need to reinvent anything to be the best version of it. You show up, you're consistent, and people count on you exactly because you never overcomplicate things.
whyItFits: The chocolate chip cookie has stayed the default American cookie for nearly a century by being exactly what it promises, every time.

title: The Nostalgic One
description: You're warm, a little old-fashioned, and genuinely happiest revisiting something familiar rather than chasing the newest thing.
whyItFits: Snickerdoodles have a slightly mysterious, folksy history and a cinnamon-sugar warmth that reads as comfort before anything else.

title: The Practical One
description: You get things done without fuss. You'd rather make something genuinely good with what's already in the pantry than wait for a special occasion.
whyItFits: The peanut butter cookie is a straightforward, no-nonsense American staple built for reliability, not spectacle.

title: The Purist
description: You believe fewer, better ingredients beat a long list every time, and you take real technique seriously.
whyItFits: Shortbread is deliberately just butter, sugar, and flour -- its whole identity rests on getting a simple ratio exactly right.

title: The Perfectionist
description: You care about precision and craft, and you'd rather do one thing exceptionally well than many things adequately.
whyItFits: Sablé is a technique-forward cookie taught explicitly for its exacting butter-to-flour ratio in French pastry training.

title: The Contradiction
description: You contain multitudes -- crisp on the outside, soft underneath, and impossible to fully predict.
whyItFits: Amaretti's whole appeal is the contrast between its crackled crisp shell and its dense, chewy interior.

title: The Warm Center
description: You seem simple at first, but there's something rich and a little unexpected once people get close.
whyItFits: A stroopwafel looks like a plain wafer until it's warmed and the caramel filling inside becomes the whole point.

title: The Sentimentalist
description: You show up for the people you love with something thoughtful and a little labor-intensive, because the effort is the point.
whyItFits: Linzer cookies are a holiday-baking staple precisely because they take real care -- rolling, cutting, filling, dusting.

title: The Storyteller
description: You carry history with you, and you'd rather share something meaningful across generations than something merely trendy.
whyItFits: Ma'amoul is tied to specific holidays across multiple faith communities and is often made as a shared family ritual, not a quick bake.

title: The Cross-Cultural Original
description: You're the product of more than one influence, and that mix is exactly what makes you interesting.
whyItFits: Nankhatai is a genuine cross-cultural invention -- Dutch and Irani baking technique adapted with local Indian ingredients like ghee and cardamom.

title: The Devoted One
description: When you commit to something, you commit fully -- there's no half-measure version of you.
whyItFits: An alfajor doesn't skimp on its dulce de leche filling -- it's thick, generous, and the entire reason the cookie exists.

title: The Steady One
description: You hold up under real pressure, and people trust you specifically because you're built to last.
whyItFits: Anzac biscuits were engineered to survive a long sea voyage without spoiling -- durability was the whole design brief.

title: The Delicate One
description: You seem sturdy from a distance, but you're actually soft and easily moved once someone gets close enough to notice.
whyItFits: A polvorón looks like a solid little cookie right up until the first bite, when it collapses into powder almost instantly.
